Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the all-important run chase! Happy faces in the Afghan camp as the players form a huddle near the ropes with Gulbadin Naib trying to pump up his teammates before striding onto the field and the umpires are out in the middle as well. It will be the pairing of Matthew Short and Travis Head that will open the innings for Australia. Azmatullah Omarzai to start proceedings with the ball, let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Australia got off to an ideal start with Spencer Johnson producing a beauty to dismiss Rahmanullah Gurbaz in the very first over. However, the pacers struggled to capitalize on that breakthrough and couldn't fully exploit the swing on offer. The spinners stepped up in the middle overs, with Adam Zampa grabbing two key wickets and Glenn Maxwell chipping in with one. Ben Dwarshuis continued his impressive form with a three-fer, but Australia might feel they let Afghanistan off the hook, especially after eyeing a sub-250 total at one stage. Conceding 37 extras could also prove costly in a high-stakes game like this. While the Aussies boast a strong batting lineup, the pressure of a knockout match is a different challenge altogether, and Afghanistan won’t make it easy. Stay tuned for the chase!

Adam Zampa is up for a quick chat. He says that it has been a mixed day for him as he struggled to find the correct length but he is satisfied that he picked up a couple of wickets in the end. Adds that the pitch is a bit two-paced and he came in to bowl in the powerplay where the ball was coming onto the bat nicely. Mention that the Afghan bowlers will bowl stumps to stumps, especially Rashid as they like to do so with the batters of Australia to protect the stumps and play out straightly to the spinners of Afghanistan. Concludes that he is pretty happy with the score and hopes that they will be able to defend it.

Despite an early setback, Afghanistan weathered the storm well, with Sediqullah Atal and Ibrahim Zadran providing stability at the crease. However, they stumbled once spin came into play, losing key wickets at crucial moments. Atal fell for 85, just when they needed him to push on for a big score. The middle order couldn't contribute much, apart from Azmatullah Omarzai, who handled the situation brilliantly, scoring a vital 67 off 63 to ensure the bowlers have something to defend when they take the field again.

Afghanistan put up a strong batting display! The momentum swung back and forth, with both teams refusing to give an inch. However, a crucial knock from the ODI Cricketer of the Year 2024, Azmatullah Omarzai, has powered them to a competitive total. That said, Australia will believe they've done well to restrict them to 15-20 runs below par on this batting-friendly surface, with dew also set to play a factor.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Ben Dwarshuis closes things out with a couple of wickets in the final over and Afghanistan are all out for 273 on the very last ball of the innings. Ben takes some pace off and bowls it into the pitch, angling it across off, Noor Ahmad backs away to cut but seems to have missed it and Josh Inglis dives forward to pouch the ball. The batters runs through for a bye and there isn't much of an appeal but the umpire says no. It is reviewed though and UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball is next to the ball and it is taken cleanly as well, so a good review and Dwarshius ends with 3 wickets.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! The inning is in a well-balanced state for both teams as of now. Afghanistan did a good recovery after losing Rahmanullah Gurbaz, and they were going great in the first powerplay, but Australia came back with spin. They squeezed up the runs and in the process, Ibrahim Zadran threw his wicket away to a not-good ball of Adam Zampa. Rahmat Shah has just come in to the crease and will look to lay down a good platform for the upcoming batters as they would want a good score of 280 plus from here. Australia just need to chip in more wickets here. An interesting passage of play is ahead of us. Adam Zampa to continue from this end.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to play! The two umpires are already out on the field of play and so are the Australian players. It will be the usual duo of Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to open the innings for Afghanistan. Spencer Johnson has the new ball in hand and is ready to steam in. A couple of slips in place to begin with, let's play...

We are just a few minutes away from the start of the action and a few of the floodlights are already on. The officials will now walk out along with the mascots before the two sets of players stride out and line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Australia first, followed by that of Afghanistan.

Steve Smith, the skipper of Australia, says that they would have bowled first anyway. He talks about the reason as the weather is unpredictable, and it can create a big difference in the end. Adds that all the boys are preparing well for this good Afghanistan team as they played brilliantly against England the other night. They are looking forward to a good contest. Mentions that this game is a must-win for them and they will come out with good intent here. Informs that they are going unchanged as well.

Hashmatullah Shahidi, the captain of Afghanistan, says that they will bat first and the wicket looks good. Adds that England and Australia have already played here and it is a slow wicket. Says that hopefully it remains the same throughout the game. Mentions that they were really happy with the win over England but they have also talked about a few things that they need to improve. Informs they are unchanged.
Australia (Unchanged XI) - Matthew Short, Travis Head, Steve Smith (C), Marnus Labuschagne, Josh Inglis (WK), Alex Carey, Glenn Maxwell, Ben Dwarshuis, Nathan Ellis, Adam Zampa, Spencer Johnson.

Afghanistan (Unchanged XI) - Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Sediqullah Atal, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Azmatullah Omarzai, Mohammad Nabi, Gulbadin Naib, Rashid Khan, Noor Ahmad, Fazalhaq Farooqi.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in favor of Afghanistan. Hashmatullah Shahidi opts to BAT first.

PITCH REPORT - Ian Bishop is pitchside. He starts by saying that there was plenty of rain last night, but the current weather is pleasant, and the chances of rainfall are reducing with every passing minute. Adds that the boundary is 73 meters to the leg side from where he is standing and 64 meters to the off side. Matthew Hayden joins him and says that the surface looks good, and it should be a run-fest, and it will be all about restraining the batters.

The pitch at Gaddafi Stadium is once again expected to be good for batting, setting up the possibility of another high-scoring thriller like the first two matches. However, the weather is unpredictable, with rain threats looming over Lahore. Given the conditions, teams may prefer to chase, as knowing the target could be crucial in a rain-affected contest. With both teams fighting for survival, expect a thrilling battle filled with twists, drama, and high stakes. Don’t go anywhere as the toss and playing XI aren’t far away!

For Afghanistan, Ibrahim Zadran and Azmatullah Omarzai have been the standout performers, leading their team to victory against England. This young and dynamic squad has shown resilience and a never-give-up attitude, making them a dangerous opposition. However, Fazalhaq Farooqi’s form is a worry, as he has struggled with both fitness and rhythm. Against a strong batting lineup like Australia, Farooqi and the rest of the pace attack will need to be at their absolute best. Afghanistan must also mentally overcome their 2023 heartbreak against Maxwell’s brilliance and focus on playing good cricket to seal their place in the semi-final.

One of the biggest positives for Australia in this tournament has been Josh Inglis’ brilliant finishing ability, which was on full display in their chase against England. Matthew Short has also been in good form, scoring a solid half-century. However, the experienced duo of Travis Head and captain Steve Smith needs to step up, especially against Afghanistan’s potent spin attack. Smith, known for his expertise against spin, will have a crucial role in countering Rashid Khan, Mohammad Nabi, and Noor Ahmad. The pace attack remains a concern, as Australia lack seasoned fast bowlers in this tournament, making Adam Zampa’s role as the lead spinner even more critical in breaking Afghanistan’s middle order.

Australia’s previous match against South Africa was washed out, leaving them with three points from two matches. This makes today’s game a must-win clash, as a loss could see them eliminated if South Africa wins their next game. If both Australia and South Africa lose their last matches, then the net run rate will come into play for the semi-final qualification. On the other side, Afghanistan’s equation is simple, a win today will send them straight into the semi-final, while a loss will knock them out of the tournament. This match, therefore, becomes a virtual knockout, with immense pressure on both teams to deliver.

Hello and welcome to Match 10 of the ICC Champions Trophy 2025, where Australia take on Afghanistan at the Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore. Afghanistan are coming into this match with sky-high confidence after a stunning win against England, and they will be eager to avenge their heartbreaking loss to Australia in the 2023 ODI World Cup, where Glenn Maxwell’s once-in-a-lifetime inning snatched victory away from them. On the other hand, Australia have had the upper hand in the last three ICC ODI World Cups, winning all three encounters. They started their campaign dominantly, successfully chasing 350+ against England, and now they look set for another strong performance. The stakes couldn't be higher, with both teams fighting for a semi-final spot.

Whenever Afghanistan and Australia face off, one memory instantly comes to mind - Glenn Maxwell’s mind-blowing double hundred in the 2023 ODI World Cup, a knock that single-handedly shattered Afghan hopes. Now, the stakes are just as high, with a semi-final spot on the line. Afghanistan come into this game brimming with confidence after a thrilling win over England, making it two ICC ODI tournament victories against them in a row. Ibrahim Zadran was the hero last time, smashing a sensational 177, while his opening partner Rahmanullah Gurbaz is due for a big knock, perhaps he’s saving it for the Aussies. The experienced Rahmat Shah adds stability, while skipper Hashmatullah Shahidi brings resilience to the middle order. All-rounders Mohammad Nabi and Azmatullah Omarzai have been crucial, with Omarzai picking up a match-winning five-wicket haul against England. Add to that Gulbadin Naib, Afghanistan’s man for the big moments, and they have a well-rounded squad ready for battle. But Afghanistan’s biggest weapon? Spin. Rashid Khan remains the ultimate game-changer, while Noor Ahmad’s rise makes their attack even deadlier. Fazalhaq Farooqi leads the pace attack but will need to step up against a strong Australian batting lineup. Afghanistan know what’s at stake - a win keeps their dream alive, and against Australia, the hunger for revenge is even greater. Australia, on the other hand, pulled off a stunning chase against England in their opener, with Josh Inglis leading the charge with a brilliant century. Matthew Short and Marnus Labuschagne chipped in as well, but the real firepower lies with Travis Head and skipper Steve Smith. If these two find their rhythm, Australia’s batting becomes a juggernaut. Alex Carey has been in red-hot form, while Maxwell, the tormentor of Afghanistan, would love to haunt them once again with his sheer power hitting. However, their bowling lineup is not at full strength, missing some key names. Spencer Johnson has big shoes to fill in Mitchell Starc’s absence, while Nathan Ellis will be crucial with his clever variations. Ben Dwarshuis provides solid support, but it’s Adam Zampa who holds the key in the middle overs with his accurate spin bowling, with Short, Maxwell, and Labuschagne also able to contribute with the ball. If Australia want an extra spin option, Tanveer Sangha could come into play. Australia don’t like leaving their fate in the hands of others, they always find a way to get the job done in ICC tournaments. A win here will seal their place in the semi-finals, but a loss could throw them into uncertainty. Can Afghanistan rise to the occasion and take down the mighty Aussies, or will Australia once again crush their dreams? We’re about to witness a battle for survival, and it promises to be an absolute thriller!
